scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer system using SiO2 and TiO2 on a glass substrate, the stacking order Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass allows for a lower arithmetic mean reflectance over 450-700 nm than the reverse order, provided the layer thicknesses are optimized within the 40-160 nm range.
expected_advantages: Smoother index transition from air to substrate may reduce peak reflectance
Deterministic TMM ensures exact solution within numerical precision
known_risks: The optimal thicknesses may lie outside the 40-160 nm constraint box
The reversed order (TiO2 first) might theoretically perform better for this specific wavelength band
Constant index assumption may introduce errors if actual materials have dispersion
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase as the optimizer converges towards the global minimum within the thickness bounds
valid_candidates should remain equal to the number of evaluated points if all thickness pairs satisfy the 40-160 nm constraint
tightest_margin should reflect the distance of the best solution from the 40 nm or 160 nm boundaries
If the hypothesis holds, the final mean reflectance should be lower than typical single-layer limits, potentially approaching the 0.03 target
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-4 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops to zero due to constraint violations (unlikely given bounded search space), stop and report failure
